items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now you mentioned Jolly Roll and Louie. Do you remember any of the other recording leaders?

ctx.x: Some of the Hot Five records I think we used as models. I can't remember exactly which ones. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Did you depend on written scores to get an idea of how the chords went? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No. At that period, most of us were sort of unfamiliar with what chords were. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And we just faked it. I mean, you know, we played entirely by ear and did the best we could. And I guess we had a lot of fun, but most of it sounded awful.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now you mentioned Jolly Roll and Louie. Do you remember any of the other recording leaders?
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, some of those small groups were Johnny Dodds. Generally the New Orleans groups we were mainly impressed with.
